questions.q: In config.ts, what happens if RPC_URL is missing from the environment when envSchema.parse(process.env) runs?
options: It fails immediately, right there, with a clear validation error — not three function calls later inside a provider constructor
It silently defaults to localhost
It compiles but crashes only when the script is deployed to production
zod automatically prompts the user to type a value
questions.explain: zod's .parse() throws immediately if the schema doesn't match, which is the whole point of validating config at startup rather than trusting process.env directly.

questions.q: In chain.ts's getChainSnapshot function, why is the address validated with isAddress BEFORE the network calls run?
options: So a malformed address never costs an RPC round-trip — it fails fast and cheaply instead of wasting a network call on bad input
Because isAddress must run after every network call, not before
Because ethers requires addresses to be validated exactly once per session
It has no real benefit, it's purely stylistic
questions.explain: Checking the address's validity before calling the network avoids an unnecessary RPC round-trip (and the resulting confusing error) for input that was never going to work.

questions.q: Why does getChainSnapshot use Promise.all for the blockNumber and balance reads instead of awaiting them one after another?
options: Because Promise.all is required syntax for any async function
Because the two reads don't depend on each other's result, so running them concurrently is strictly faster than awaiting them sequentially
Because ethers does not allow sequential awaits
Because Promise.all automatically retries failed calls
questions.explain: getBlockNumber and getBalance are independent reads; Promise.all lets both RPC calls happen concurrently rather than waiting for one to finish before starting the other.

questions.q: Why doesn't index.ts need a try/catch block wrapped around its call to getChainSnapshot?
options: Because getChainSnapshot already converts every possible failure into a Result<T>, so index.ts only needs to check result.ok instead of catching a thrown exception
Because TypeScript doesn't support try/catch inside async functions
Because network calls can never fail once an address passes isAddress
Because main() automatically wraps every line in its own try/catch
questions.explain: chain.ts's Result<T> pattern (from Lesson 28) means failures are returned as data (`{ ok: false, error }`), not thrown — so the caller just checks `result.ok` rather than needing its own try/catch.

questions.q: Which earlier lesson's exact pattern does index.ts's `process.argv[2]` + `main().catch(...)` structure come from?
options: Lesson 36's Express error-handling middleware
Lesson 35's fs/promises caching
Lesson 33's script entry-point, process.argv, and exit-code pattern
Lesson 31's REPL
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly ties index.ts's structure back to Lesson 33's main()/process.argv/process.exit pattern for building a real, tool-friendly script.
